observations.raw_text: I switched from Notion because I got tired of my notes being in someone else's cloud. I need to own my data. Period.
observations.extracted_intent: Wants local data storage and ownership
observations.inferred_need: Deep anxiety about data sovereignty; needs confidence that their intellectual property is not accessible to third parties

observations.raw_text: We evaluated 8 tools last quarter. Shipped features for 6 of them. Two actually moved metrics. The other 4 were a waste. We had no framework to say no earlier.
observations.extracted_intent: Wants a framework to filter candidates before building
observations.inferred_need: Judgment bottleneck — cannot distinguish high-impact from low-impact candidates before committing engineering resources

observations.raw_text: Our PM team of 5 each has their own prioritization spreadsheet. When we need to decide what to cut, it becomes political. There's no shared framework.
observations.extracted_intent: Wants a unified prioritization system across the PM team
observations.inferred_need: Kill decisions are avoided because there's no objective, shared basis for them. Constitution-based reasoning could depoliticize the process

observations.raw_text: AI coding tools let us prototype in hours. But now we have 15 prototypes and no idea which 3 to actually invest in. The decision backlog is worse than the dev backlog ever was.
observations.extracted_intent: Overproduction of prototypes, needs decision support
observations.inferred_need: AI-accelerated production has created a judgment bottleneck; needs systematic allocation, not more ideation

observations.raw_text: I want my team to collaborate in real-time. Async is too slow for us. We need everyone seeing the same board, same data, same decisions, live.
observations.extracted_intent: Wants real-time collaboration features
observations.inferred_need: Team alignment through shared visibility; reducing communication overhead in fast-moving teams

observations.raw_text: We don't need another AI that tells us what to build. We need something that helps us explain why we're NOT building something. My CEO keeps asking 'why did we kill that?' and I can't point to anything concrete.
observations.extracted_intent: Needs kill reasoning documentation
observations.inferred_need: Organizational accountability for kill decisions; evidence-based justification that survives executive challenge

observations.raw_text: The offline thing is huge for me. I travel a lot, I'm on planes, I can't depend on cloud. If it doesn't work offline, I don't use it.
observations.extracted_intent: Requires offline functionality
observations.inferred_need: Workflow continuity regardless of connectivity; offline-first is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have

observations.raw_text: I'd pay $200/month if it could tell me which of our 20 feature candidates to kill, with evidence I can show to stakeholders. Right now I spend a full week every quarter on prioritization theater.
observations.extracted_intent: Willing to pay for evidence-based kill decisions
observations.inferred_need: Time savings on prioritization + political cover for difficult kill decisions; $200/mo signals serious pain

observations.raw_text: Feature: offline_sync — 78% of active users enable offline mode within first week. Retention for offline-enabled users: 85% at D30 vs 45% for cloud-only users.
observations.extracted_intent: Offline mode has high adoption and correlates with retention
observations.inferred_need: Offline capability is a core retention driver, not a peripheral feature

observations.raw_text: Feature: social_activity_feed — only 12% of users interact with it. Of those, 60% disable it within 2 weeks. Top complaint in settings: 'too noisy'.
observations.extracted_intent: Social activity feed has low adoption and high churn
observations.inferred_need: Users actively reject social/visibility features; this conflicts with privacy-first positioning

observations.raw_text: Feature: ai_suggestion_panel — 45% click-through on first exposure, drops to 8% by day 7. Users who disable it have higher D30 retention (72%) than users who keep it (58%).
observations.extracted_intent: AI suggestion feature has novelty effect but hurts retention
observations.inferred_need: Unsolicited AI suggestions feel intrusive to focus-oriented users; feature may violate quality_bar (simplicity over feature count)

observations.raw_text: Feature: team_dashboard — 92% of teams with 3+ members use it daily. Correlates with 2.3x higher expansion revenue. Top request: 'make the kill/defer reasons visible to the whole team'.
observations.extracted_intent: Team dashboard is a power feature for multi-PM teams
observations.inferred_need: Shared visibility into decisions is the killer feature for growth-stage teams; aligns with collaboration-first positioning

observations.raw_text: Onboarding funnel: signup (100%) → constitution_input (68%) → first_pipeline_run (41%) → evidence_drilldown (22%) → execution_packet (9%). Biggest drop: constitution_input → first_pipeline_run.
observations.extracted_intent: Major onboarding drop-off after constitution input
observations.inferred_need: Users write constitution but don't proceed to pipeline; either import step is too heavy, or they don't understand what happens next

observations.raw_text: Feature: real_time_collab — 88% adoption in teams >5 people. Average session overlap: 3.2 concurrent users. But solo founders never use it (0% adoption for team_size=1).
observations.extracted_intent: Real-time collaboration is essential for teams, irrelevant for solos
observations.inferred_need: Collaboration features scale with team size; solo founders need a different value proposition (judgment support, not collaboration)

observations.raw_text: Feature: analytics_tracking — 34% of users opt out of anonymous usage analytics. Among privacy-tech companies, opt-out rate is 89%.
observations.extracted_intent: Privacy-conscious users reject analytics
observations.inferred_need: Any telemetry, even anonymous, is a deal-breaker for privacy-focused segment. Zero-telemetry-by-default is a trust requirement

observations.raw_text: Love the concept but the app is useless without internet. I was on a flight and couldn't access my notes. Deleted it.
observations.extracted_intent: App requires internet; user deleted due to lack of offline
observations.inferred_need: Offline access is not a feature request — it's a retention cliff. No offline = immediate churn for mobile-heavy users

observations.raw_text: Why does a productivity app need access to my contacts? Instant uninstall. No trust.
observations.extracted_intent: Excessive permissions destroy trust
observations.inferred_need: Permission requests must be minimal and justified; any perception of data harvesting triggers immediate churn

observations.raw_text: 5 stars. Finally a tool that doesn't try to do everything. It does one thing — helps me focus — and does it perfectly. Don't add more features please.
observations.extracted_intent: User values simplicity and focus
observations.inferred_need: Feature restraint is a competitive advantage for this segment; adding features would violate the quality_bar clause

observations.raw_text: The AI features feel forced. I didn't ask for suggestions while writing. It breaks my flow. Let me turn them off or I'm leaving.
observations.extracted_intent: AI suggestions disrupt user flow
observations.inferred_need: Unsolicited AI intervention violates the 'deep focus' value. AI features must be opt-in, not opt-out

observations.raw_text: Great for solo use but terrible for teams. Can't share a board, can't see what others decided. We need team visibility.
observations.extracted_intent: No team collaboration features
observations.inferred_need: Solo-first design limits growth into team segment. Team visibility is required for PM teams of 3+

observations.raw_text: I love that my data stays on my device. This is how all productivity tools should work. Take my money.
observations.extracted_intent: Values local data storage
observations.inferred_need: Local-first is a purchasing trigger, not just a preference. Willingness to pay is directly linked to data sovereignty

observations.raw_text: Notification spam killed it for me. I turned off notifications and forgot the app existed. Engagement tricks don't work on people who want focus.
observations.extracted_intent: Notification-driven engagement backfires
observations.inferred_need: Engagement-maximizing patterns are anti-correlated with retention in focus-oriented segment. Forbidden pattern violation

observations.raw_text: I exported my data as CSV but it doesn't include my tags or folder structure. The export is useless without metadata. I feel trapped.
observations.extracted_intent: Data export is incomplete
observations.inferred_need: Data portability is a trust requirement. Incomplete export feels like vendor lock-in, violating the trust_compliance_rule

observations.raw_text: Your pricing page says 'free for individuals' but I hit a paywall after 10 documents. That's not free. That's a dark pattern.
observations.extracted_intent: Perceived bait-and-switch in pricing
observations.inferred_need: Pricing transparency is a trust issue. Artificial limits on free tier feel like a dark pattern — explicit constitution violation

observations.raw_text: How do I integrate with Cursor? I want to pipe your execution packets directly into my coding agent. Is there an API?
observations.extracted_intent: Wants API for coding agent integration
observations.inferred_need: Builder handoff is a real workflow need. Execution packet → coding agent pipeline is not hypothetical, users are asking for it

observations.raw_text: Pipeline takes 45 seconds. By the time results come in I've already context-switched. Can you make it faster or at least show progress?
observations.extracted_intent: Pipeline latency is too high
observations.inferred_need: Interactive speed (< 15s) is required for the tool to fit into PM workflow. Streaming/progress indicators are table stakes

observations.raw_text: The kill reasoning said 'violates prohibited_business_model' but my constitution says 'we never compromise on quality'. That's not a business model violation. The clause mapping is wrong.
observations.extracted_intent: Constitution normalization produced incorrect clause mapping
observations.inferred_need: Constitution parser accuracy is critical. Misattributed clauses undermine trust in the entire system (H-4 risk)

observations.raw_text: I changed my constitution and re-ran the pipeline but 3 out of 5 results were identical. I expected everything to change. Is it actually using my constitution?
observations.extracted_intent: Constitution change didn't visibly affect results
observations.inferred_need: Constitution must demonstrably impact output. If changes don't produce visible differences, users lose trust in the mechanism

observations.raw_text: Hot take: the PM tools market is about to bifurcate. Half will be 'generate more ideas' (Productboard AI, ChatPRD). The other half will be 'kill more ideas' (BONSAI-style). The second half wins.
observations.extracted_intent: Market observer sees kill-first as differentiation
observations.inferred_need: Category positioning validation — 'kill-first' resonates as contrarian but defensible market position

observations.raw_text: Every PM tool is adding AI now. If your moat is just 'we use Claude to prioritize', you'll be a feature in Productboard by Q3.
observations.extracted_intent: AI PM tools are commoditizing
observations.inferred_need: LLM wrapper risk is real. Differentiation must come from the constitutional framework, not from the LLM call itself

observations.raw_text: We use Notion + a spreadsheet + gut feeling. It works okay for 10 candidates. But we now have 40 and the spreadsheet is chaos. I need something that scales beyond gut.
observations.extracted_intent: Current method breaks at scale
observations.inferred_need: Switching trigger is at ~20+ candidates. Below that, spreadsheet + intuition is 'good enough'. BONSAI's value starts at scale

observations.raw_text: What I really want is a way to explain to my CEO why we killed something. Not 'I felt it wasn't right' but 'here are 12 pieces of evidence and 2 constitutional violations'. That's what gets me political cover.
observations.extracted_intent: Needs evidence-backed kill justification for executive communication
observations.inferred_need: Kill reasoning is not just analytical — it's organizational ammunition. The value is in making difficult decisions defensible

observations.raw_text: Feature: gamification_badges — 5% adoption after 30 days. Users who interact with badges have 20% lower NPS than non-interactors. Negative correlation with focus_mode usage.
observations.extracted_intent: Gamification hurts NPS and conflicts with focus features
observations.inferred_need: Gamification is anti-correlated with the core value proposition (deep focus). Classic constitutional_misalignment candidate

observations.raw_text: Feature: export_to_linear — 67% of execution_packet viewers click 'export to Linear/Jira'. But only 12% complete the export. Blocker: authentication flow for external tools.
observations.extracted_intent: High intent for external tool integration, blocked by auth
observations.inferred_need: Execution packet → external tool pipeline has strong demand. MVP should support copy-paste export even without native integration

observations.raw_text: Feature: notification_digest — sent daily to 100% of users. Open rate: 8%. Click-through: 2%. Unsubscribe requests: 340 in past month (12% of MAU).
observations.extracted_intent: Daily notifications are unwanted
observations.inferred_need: Push-based engagement is rejected by this user base. Any notification strategy must be pull-based or severely limited

observations.raw_text: Tried to use this for my team of 8. The lack of role-based access is a non-starter. I can't have junior PMs overriding kill decisions made by the Head of Product.
observations.extracted_intent: Needs role-based access control
observations.inferred_need: Team features require permission hierarchy. Kill override authority should map to organizational authority

observations.raw_text: The kill board is brilliant. Never seen another tool that shows you what NOT to build with actual evidence. This is what product management has been missing.
observations.extracted_intent: Kill board is a differentiating feature
observations.inferred_need: Kill-first framing resonates strongly. This is not just a feature but a category-defining positioning

observations.raw_text: Constitution concept is cool but writing 'We are / We never / We value' took me 45 minutes. By then I was frustrated and didn't finish onboarding.
observations.extracted_intent: Constitution writing is a barrier to onboarding
observations.inferred_need: Constitution input needs guided assistance. Templates, examples, or dialog-based extraction could reduce friction (H-10 pivot option)

observations.raw_text: Can I import my Productboard feedback? I have 2000 pieces of feedback there and I'm not re-entering them manually.
observations.extracted_intent: Wants Productboard data import
observations.inferred_need: Migration path from existing tools is critical for adoption. CSV/JSON import is minimum; native integrations are post-MVP

observations.raw_text: The execution packet is great but it's too abstract. 'Improve onboarding flow' — how? I need specific UI mockup descriptions, not generic directions.
observations.extracted_intent: Execution packet lacks specificity
observations.inferred_need: Execution packets must be actionable enough for engineers to start coding. Generic descriptions fail H-6 (Execution Packet usability)

observations.raw_text: The real Cursor for PM isn't about generating PRDs. It's about having a system that says 'don't build that, and here's why' with the same confidence that a test suite says 'don't ship that'.
observations.extracted_intent: Community frames kill-first allocation as the true 'Cursor for PM'
observations.inferred_need: Market narrative aligns with BONSAI positioning. Kill confidence ≈ test confidence is a powerful analogy

observations.raw_text: Shipped 3 features this week with Cursor. None of them were in our roadmap. We just... built what felt exciting. Now I'm not sure any of them matter.
observations.extracted_intent: AI-accelerated building without judgment framework
observations.inferred_need: Overproduction without allocation is the core pain. This person is the BONSAI target user

observations.raw_text: Show me the evidence trail. If I can click on a kill decision and see the exact customer quotes that led to it, that's worth the subscription alone.
observations.extracted_intent: Evidence drill-down is a key value driver
observations.inferred_need: Traceability from decision → theme → raw observation is the trust mechanism. This is how PM builds confidence in the system

observations.raw_text: We had a PM leave last month. All his prioritization context left with him. The new PM is starting from scratch. If we had a constitution and decision history, onboarding would be 10x faster.
observations.extracted_intent: Knowledge loss when PMs leave
observations.inferred_need: Constitution + decision log as organizational memory. Value increases over time as decisions accumulate — this is the moat (H-14)

observations.raw_text: Feature: dark_mode — 72% adoption. No correlation with retention or NPS. Purely aesthetic preference. Zero impact on core metrics.
observations.extracted_intent: Dark mode is popular but doesn't impact outcomes
observations.inferred_need: Hygiene feature. Should not be prioritized over features that move core metrics. Good defer candidate

observations.raw_text: Feature: weekly_email_summary — open rate 45%, click-through 22%. Users who engage with weekly summary have 1.8x higher D60 retention. Top clicked section: 'decisions made this week'.
observations.extracted_intent: Weekly summary drives retention via decision visibility
observations.inferred_need: Passive decision visibility (pull, not push) works. Weekly cadence > daily spam. 'Decisions made' section validates the decision log feature

observations.raw_text: I tried explaining the 'constitution' concept to my team and they looked at me like I was crazy. The naming is too academic. Just call it 'product policy' or 'team principles'.
observations.extracted_intent: Constitution naming is confusing for teams
observations.inferred_need: Go-to-market naming matters. 'Constitution' resonates with founders but alienates PMs. Consider 'Product Policy' for external messaging

observations.raw_text: This replaced our quarterly planning. We used to spend 2 weeks in meetings deciding what to build. Now it takes 2 hours with BONSAI and the decisions are better because they're evidence-based.
observations.extracted_intent: Massive time savings on planning
observations.inferred_need: 10x speed claim validated (2 weeks → 2 hours). This is the H-12 success signal. Quote this in the pitch

observations.raw_text: I uploaded our interview transcripts but the extraction missed nuance. It said the user 'wants faster export' but actually they were expressing frustration about data lock-in. The says vs wants detection needs work.
observations.extracted_intent: Extract step misses nuance in says-vs-wants
observations.inferred_need: Counterfactual extraction quality is critical. If says/wants is wrong, the entire pipeline is polluted. This is a core quality issue

observations.raw_text: The AI PM tools are splitting into two camps: ones that help you build more (Lovable, Rork, v0) and ones that help you build less but better (BONSAI). I'm betting on 'build less'.
observations.extracted_intent: Market sees BONSAI in 'build less' camp
observations.inferred_need: Positioning clarity: BONSAI is not 'build more with AI' but 'decide better with AI'. This distinction is the go-to-market message
